S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Sector Information
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: Additional textual information about a light sector.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Sector Limit
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. The sector limit specifies the limits of the sector In a clockwise direction around the central feature (for example a light).

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Sector Limit One
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. Sector limit one specifies the first limit of the sector. The order of sector limit one and sector limit two is clockwise around the central feature (for example a light).

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Sector Limit Two
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. Sector limit two specifies the second limit of the sector. The order of sector limit one and sector limit two is clockwise around the central feature (for example a light).

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Shape Information
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: Textual information about the shape of a non-standard topmark.
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:remarks: No formatting of text is possible within shape information. If formatted text is required, then an associated text file referenced by the complex attribute textual description must be used.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Signal Sequence
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The sequence of times occupied by intervals of light/sound and eclipse/silence for all “light characteristics” or sound signals.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Source Indication
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: Information about the source document, publication, or reference from which object data or textual material included or referenced in a dataset are derived.
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:remarks: Content of featureName is source authority name.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Spatial Accuracy
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: Provides an indication of the vertical and horizontal positional uncertainty of bathymetric data, optionally within a specified date range.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Speed
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: Rate of motion. The terms speed and velocity are often used interchangeably, but speed is a scalar, having magnitude only, while velocity is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Surface Characteristics
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The general nature of the material of which the land surface or the seabed is composed.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Survey Date Range
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The complex attribute describes the period of the hydrographic survey, as the time between its sub-attributes.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Telecommunications
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: A means or channel of communicating at a distance by electrical or electromagnetic means such as telegraphy, telephony, or broadcasting.
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:remarks: If no value is populated for the sub-attribute telecommunication service, this means the service is by voice communication. If no value is populated for the sub-attribute telecommunication carrier, this means the service is by land line communication.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Tidal Stream Panel Values
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The direction of the flow and the tidal current rate from 6 hours before to 6 hours after high water (HW) or low water (LW) at the reference tide station, at hourly or sub-hourly intervals.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Tidal Stream Value
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: A measurement of the direction and speed of a tidal stream at a given time relative to the reference tide.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Time Intervals by Day of Week
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The regular weekly operation times of a service or schedule.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Topmark
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: A characteristic shape secured at the top of a buoy or beacon to aid in its identification.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Vertical Clearance Closed
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The vertical clearance of a feature in closed condition (for example a closed lifting bridge) measured from the horizontal plane towards the feature overhead.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Vertical Clearance Fixed
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The vertical clearance measured from the horizontal plane towards a fixed (non-opening) feature overhead.
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:remarks: Vertical clearance fixed must not be used to populate authorized safe clearances.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Vertical Clearance Open
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The vertical clearance of a feature in opened condition (for example an open lifting bridge) measured from the horizontal plane towards the feature overhead.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Vertical Clearance Safe
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The safe vertical clearance of a feature measured from the horizontal plane towards the feature overhead.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Vertical Uncertainty
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The best estimate of the vertical accuracy of depths, heights, vertical distances and vertical clearances.
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:remarks: Encodes the vertical uncertainty associated with any vertical measurement.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Vessel Speed Limit
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The maximum allowed rate of travel for a vessel in an area in knots.

S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:name: Zone of Confidence
S100FC:S100_FC_ComplexAttribute.S100FC:definition: The overall indication of the quality of bathymetric data within an area based on the positional accuracy, survey equipment and coverage; optionally within a specified data range.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Auxiliary Feature
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to incidental, secondary or supplementary features related to the referenced feature.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Cartographic Text
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to a specific cartographically positioned location for text.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Collection
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to the aggregate in a whole-part relationship.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Component
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to a part in a whole-part relationship.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Equipment
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to the feature(s) supported by a structure feature.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Information
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to an object that provides more information about the referencing feature or information type.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Position Provider
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to a specific feature(s).

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Primary Feature
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to a feature to which incidental, secondary or supplementary features are related.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Quality Information
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to an information type providing spatial quality information.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Roofed Structure
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to a supported roofed structure.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Structure
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to the feature that equipment feature(s) are supported by.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Support
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to the feature(s) that support a structure.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Update
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to a feature that describes changes made to a dataset.

S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:name: The Updated Object
S100FC:S100_FC_Role.S100FC:definition: A pointer to a feature that has been updated.

S100FC:S100_FC_InformationAssociation.S100FC:name: Additional information
S100FC:S100_FC_InformationAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between at least one instance of a geo feature and an instance of an information type.

S100FC:S100_FC_InformationAssociation.S100FC:name: Quality of bathymetric data composition
S100FC:S100_FC_InformationAssociation.S100FC:definition: The mandatory association between the quality-related characteristics of bathymetric data and the horizontal position and vertical uncertainties of the data.

S100FC:S100_FC_InformationAssociation.S100FC:name: Spatial Association
S100FC:S100_FC_InformationAssociation.S100FC:definition: An association for the binding between a spatial type and its spatial quality information.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Anchorage or berth aggreation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between an anchorage area, anchor berth or berth and the related features, e.g. notice marks, mooring facilities and bollards.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Barrage association
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a barrage and its elements.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Bridge arch association
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between the individual Span Fixed features of a bridge arch.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Depth and clearance indicator association
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a Waterway Gauge and the related depth indicators or vertical clearance indicators or between several indicators.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Exceptional Navigation Structure aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a Waterway Gauge and the related depth indicators or vertical clearance indicators or between several indicators.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Lock aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between the lock and the lock basins, lock basin parts, lock gates, signal stations, waiting berths and other features.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Notice mark aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between notice marks and the features that they define.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Overhead cable aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a cable overhead and the associated pylons, notice marks, waterway gauges.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Overhead pipeline aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a pipeline overhead and the associated pylons, notice marks, waterway gauges.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Signal station aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between traffic and warning signal stations and the features to which they are related.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Tunnel aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a tunnel with a waterway in it and the associated objects, e.g. Communication Area, Notice Mark, Restricted Area, fender, Vertical clearance indicator, depth indicator, traffic signal station, warning signal station, radio calling-in point, overhead cable, overhead pipeline, waterway gauge.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Aids to navigation association
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between navigational aids and the traffic systems (such as routeing measures) that they define.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Bridge aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a bridge and its component features.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Caution area association
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a caution area and the traffic systems (such as routeing measures) to which the cautionary information applies.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Fairway aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between related fairways comprising a fairway system.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Fairway auxiliary
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a fairway and related features auxiliary to the fairway.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Mooring trot aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a mooring trot and its component parts.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Pilotage District Association
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a pilotage district and its component pilot boarding places.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Roofed Structure Aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a roofed structure over navigable water and its supporting features.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Structure/equipment
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a navigation aid equipment feature and the structure that supports it.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Text association
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a geo feature and the cartographically positioned location for text.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Traffic Separation Scheme aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a Traffic Separation Scheme or a Traffic Separation Scheme System and its component features.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Two-way route aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between a two-way route and its component features.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Update Aggregation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between an Update Information feature and its component Update Information features.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:name: Updated Information
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureAssociation.S100FC:definition: A feature association for the binding between an update information metadata feature and updated feature(s) that it identifies.

S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:name: Contact Details
S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:definition: Information on how to reach a person or organisation by postal, internet, telephone, telex and radio systems.

S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:name: Service Hours
S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:definition: The time when a service is available and known exceptions.

S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:name: Non-Standard Working Day
S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:definition: Days when many services are not available. Often days of festivity or recreation or public holidays when normal working hours are limited, especially a national or religious festival, etc.

S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:name: Nautical Information
S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:definition: Nautical information about a related area or facility.

S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:name: Spatial Quality
S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:definition: The indication of the quality of the locational information for features in a dataset.

S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:name: Time Schedule - In General
S100FC:S100_FC_InformationType.S100FC:definition: A schedule listing events and the times at which they will take place.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Quality of Non-Bathymetric Data
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area within which a uniform assessment of the quality of the non-bathymetric data exists.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Data Coverage
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A geographical area that describes the coverage and extent of spatial objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Navigational System of Marks
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area within which the navigational system of marks has been established in relation to a specific direction.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Local Direction of Buoyage
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area within which the navigational system of marks has been established in relation to a specific direction.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Quality of Bathymetric Data
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area within which a uniform assessment of the quality of the bathymetric data exists.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Sounding Datum
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The horizontal plane or tidal datum to which soundings have been reduced. Also called datum for sounding reduction. (Adapted from IHO Dictionary - S-32). The Sounding Datum for inland waterways is in most cases not a horizontal plane but a sloping plane.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Vertical Datum of Data
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Any level surface (for example Mean Sea Level) taken as a surface of reference to which the elevations within a data set are reduced. Also called datum level, reference level, reference plane, levelling datum, datum for heights. (Adapted from IHO Dictionary - S-32). The Vertical Datum of Data for inland waterways is in most cases not a horizontal plane but a sloping plane.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Quality of Survey
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area within which a uniform assessment of the reliability of source survey information exists.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Update Information
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The Update Information metadata feature is used to represent a change to the information shown.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Magnetic Variation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The angle between the magnetic and geographic meridians at any place, expressed in degrees east or west to indicate the direction of magnetic north from true north. Also called magnetic declination.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Coastline
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The line where shore and water meet. Shoreline and coastline are generally used synonymously. (IHO Dictionary - S-32). The official name 'Coastline' is a synonym for the term 'shoreline' commonly used in inland navigation.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Land Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The solid portion of the Earth's surface, as opposed to sea, water.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Land Elevation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An elevation is the vertical distance of a point or a level, on, or affixed to, the surface of the earth, measured from a specified vertical datum.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Used to encode both spot heights and land (height) contours.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: River
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A relatively large natural stream of water. (IHO Dictionary - S-32) This feature is used for non-navigable rivers.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Lake
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A large body of water entirely surrounded by land.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Land Region
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area of natural or cultivated scenery defined by its geographical characteristics and may be known by its proper name. (Adapted from S-57 Edition 3.1, Appendix A - Chapter 1, Page 1.92, November 2000). For IENCs: Land Areas adjacent to the waterway that are significant for navigation reference.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Vegetation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Plants collectively or individually, especially those dominating a particular area or habitat.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Sloping Ground
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An inclined surface. (S-57 Edition 3.1, Appendix A - Chapter 1, Page 1.161, November 2000).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Slope Topline
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The upper marking of a slope, for example the ridge line or the separation line between two different gradients. (S-57 Edition 3.1, Appendix A - Chapter 1, Page 1.160, November 2000).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Tideway
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A channel through which a tidal current runs. A natural water course in intertidal areas where water flows during the ebb or flood can also be encoded as Tideway (TIDEWY) in IENCs.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Built-Up Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area of land or construction over the water containing a concentration of buildings and/or other structures.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Building
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A free-standing self-supporting construction that is roofed, usually walled, and is intended for human occupancy (for example: a place of work or recreation) and/or habitation. For IENCs: Buildings with a special function, which may be of interest for the boatmaster.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: This feature is used to encode single buildings, including those with a particular function or service of major interest.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Airport/Airfield
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A defined area on land (including any buildings, installations and equipment) intended to be used either wholly or in part for the arrival, departure and surface movement of aircraft.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Runway
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A defined area, on a land aerodrome, prepared for the landing and take-off run of aircraft.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Helipad
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A small landing surface for helicopters, with minimal or no supporting installations or facilities.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Typically a small paved, metallic, or other type of prepared surface intended for landings and takeoffs by a single helicopter, and generally without specialised supporting technical or administrative facilities as provided in heliports and airports.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Bridge
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: (1) An elevated structure extending across or over the weather deck of a vessel, or part of such a structure. The term is sometimes modified to indicate the intended use, such as navigating bridge or signal bridge. (2) A structure erected over a depression or an obstacle such as a body of water, railroad, etc., to provide a roadway for vehicles or pedestrians.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A bridge may consist of portions which cover the land and the water.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Span Fixed
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A fixed component of the deck of a bridge spanning successive bridge piers.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Span Opening
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An opening component of the deck of a bridge spanning successive bridge piers.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Conveyor
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A mechanical device for conveying bulk material or people using an endless moving belt or series of rollers.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Cable Overhead
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A single continuous rope-like bundle consisting of multiple strands of fiber, plastic, metal, and/or glass, which is supported by structures such as poles or pylons and passing over or nearby navigable waters.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The cable supports are encoded as separate pylon/bridge support features.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Pipeline Overhead
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A string of interconnected pipes, supported by pylons and passing over or nearby navigable waters, used for the transport of matter, nowadays mainly oil or gas.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A pipeline is a string of interconnected pipes used for the transport of matter, nowadays mainly oil or gas (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 3857).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Pylon/Bridge Support
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A vertical construction consisting, for example, of a steel framework or pre-stressed concrete to carry cables, a bridge, etc.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Fence/Wall
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A man-made barrier used as an enclosure or boundary or for protection.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Railway
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A rail or set of parallel rails on which a train, tram, or rail wagon runs.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Road
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A route with a specially prepared surface that is intended for use by wheeled vehicles or pedestrians.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Tunnel
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A passage that is open to the atmosphere at both ends, buried under the seabed or laid over the seafloor or bored under the ground or through mountains.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Landmark
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Any prominent object at a fixed location on land which can be used in determining a location or a direction.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Silo/Tank
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A large storage structure used for storing loose materials, liquids and/or gases.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Wind Turbine
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A tower and associated equipment that generates electrical power from wind. They can be sited offshore and may be either fixed or floating.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Fortified Structure
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A structure that is specifically designed or reinforced to provide for defence from armed attack.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A fortified structure is often disused, decayed or used for non-defence purpose. Such structures range from major castles and forts to minor lookout posts.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Production/Storage Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area on land for the exploitation or storage of natural resources.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Checkpoint
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An official location at which to register, declare and/or inspect goods and/or people.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The object 'checkpoint' does not include facilities such as buildings, gates or other installations.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Hulk
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The hull of a wrecked or condemned ship, from which the fittings and superstructure have usually been removed, which is moored in a permanent position or grounded. It may be abandoned or put to some other use.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Pile
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A long heavy timber or section of steel, wood, concrete, etc., forced into the earth or seafloor to serve as a support, as for a pier, or to resist lateral pressure; or as a free standing pole within a marine environment.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Dyke
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A dyke (or dike) is an artificial embankment to contain or hold back water.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Shoreline Construction
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A fixed artificial structure in the water and/or adjoining the land. It may also refer to features such as training walls, which are not necessarily connected to, nor form part of the shoreline. For IENCs Shoreline Construction includes groins, ground sills, revetments, training walls, boat ramps, slipways, docks, wharfs, lock walls, ice breakers, water intake structures, fenders, landing steps and ladders.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Structure Over Navigable Water
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A roofed structure erected, or partly erected, over a body of water, to provide protection for a vessel or its cargo.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Causeway
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A raised way across low or wet ground or water.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Canal
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An artificial waterway with no flow, or a controlled flow, used for navigation, or for draining or irrigating land (ditch). This feature is only used for non-navigable canals in Inland ENCs.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Distance Mark
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A distance mark indicates the distance measured from an origin and consists of either a solid visible structure or a distinct location without special installation. Usually found on canals. On inland waterway it is used to serve as a reference along the waterway. Due to natural or historic changes in the waterway, the distance can deviate from real distance to the origin.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Gate
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A structure that may be swung, drawn, or lowered to block an entrance or passageway on a watercourse.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Used to encode gates that control the flow of water.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Dam
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A barrier to check or confine anything in motion; particularly one constructed to hold back water and raise its level to form a reservoir, or to prevent flooding.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Crane
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A machine for lifting, shifting and lowering objects or materials by means of a swinging boom or with a lifting apparatus supported on an overhead track.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The position of a sheerlegs or a travelling crane is defined as its resting position.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Berth
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A place, generally named or numbered, where a vessel may moor or anchor. For IENCs: A designated named or numbered place at the bank of the river or in a harbour basin for the mooring of vessels

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Dolphin
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A post or group of posts, used for mooring or warping a vessel, or as an aid to navigation. The dolphin may be in the water, on a wharf or on the beach.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Bollard
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Small shaped post, mounted on a wharf or dolphin used to secure ship's lines.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Dry Dock
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An artificial basin fitted with a gate or caisson, into which vessels can be floated and the water pumped out to expose the vessel's bottom. Also called graving dock.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Floating Dock
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A form of dry dock consisting of a floating structure of one or more sections which can be partly submerged by controlled flooding to receive a vessel, then raised by pumping out the water so that the vessel's bottom can be exposed.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Pontoon
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A floating structure, usually rectangular in shape which serves as landing, pier head, bridge support, etc.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Dock Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An artificially enclosed area within which ships may moor and which may have gates to regulate water level.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Gridiron
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A structure in the intertidal zone serving as a support for vessels at low stages of the tide to permit work on the exposed portion of the vessel's hull.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Lock Basin
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A wet dock in a waterway, permitting a ship to pass from one level to another.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Mooring Trot
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A mooring is a place where a vessel may be secured. A mooring trot is a mooring that is composed of ground tackle, mooring cables, buoys and mooring berths on junction cables.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Sea Area/Named Water Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A geographically defined part of the sea or other navigable waters. It may be specified within its limits by its proper name.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Each sea area is defined independent of any other. Smaller sea areas may be located within larger sea areas.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Tidal Stream - Flood/Ebb
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Approximate tidal stream rates given as discrete rate values for flood and ebb flow during springs. For IENCs tThe alternating horizontal movement of water associated with the rise and fall of the tide caused by tide-producing forces. Also called tidal current.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A tidal stream (or tidal current) is a horizontal movement of water associated with the rise and fall of the tide caused by tide-producing forces.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Current - Non-Gravitational
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Any current that is caused by other than tide producing forces. For IENCs Current is preferably indicated at high and low water conditions to aid with planning, navigation and maneuvering.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Non-gravitational currents include either singly or in combination: ocean currents (wind and/or density driven), inter-oceanic equalizing currents, currents of navigable rivers, river outflow effects offshore and other non-tidal flows.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Water Turbulence
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The disturbance of water caused by the interaction of any combination of waves, currents, tidal streams, wind, shoal patches and obstructions.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Tidal Stream Panel Data
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Approximate tidal stream characteristics given as discrete value sets at a specified interval before and/or after a high or low water.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A tidal stream (or tidal current) is an alternating horizontal movement of water associated with the rise and fall of the tide caused by tide-producing forces.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Sounding
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Measured or charted depth of water (may be a drying height), or the measurement of such a depth, which has been reduced to a vertical datum.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Drying heights (drying soundings) are indicated by a negative value.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Dredged Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area of the bottom of a body of water which has been deepened by dredging.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Depth Contour
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A line connecting points of equal water depth which is sometimes significantly displaced outside of soundings, symbols, and other chart detail for clarity as well as generalization. Depth contours therefore often represent an approximate location of the line of equal depth as related to the surveyed line delineated on the source. For IENCs a line of constant depth denoting the depth between Shallow Depth and Fairway / Project Depth
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Drying contours are encoded with negative values.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Depth Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A water area whose depth is within a defined range of values. For IENCs detailed depth information (surface): - either referred to one reference water level only: water surface within the waterway whose detailed depth information is within a defined range of values that refer to only one vertical datum, the reference water level. or - referred to a water level model that is applied to Depth Areas: a water surface within the waterway in which detailed depth information is known within a defined range of values referenced to a vertical datum (the reference water level). The actual water level is provided by a water level model.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Intertidal areas are encoded as depth areas. These do not have to include soundings. The depth range within a depth area is defined by the attributes depth range maximum value and depth range minimum value.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Unsurveyed Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area where hydrographic survey data is non-existent.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Seabed Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A region of the seabed including the material of which it is composed and its physical characteristics. Also called nature of bottom, character (or characteristics) of the bottom, or quality of the bottom.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Generally, it is not possible to define a seabed area by its real extent. For that reason, the characteristics of the seabed area may be represented at one single position.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Weed/Kelp
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Any macroscopic marine alga.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Seagrass
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Any of various submerged monocotyledonous plants (such as eelgrass, tape grass, and turtle grass) of tropical to temperate usually shallow coastal waters that have narrow grass-like leaves and often form dense underwater meadows.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Sandwave
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A large mobile wave-like sediment feature in shallow water and composed of sand. The wavelength may reach 100 metres, the amplitude may be up to 20 metres.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Underwater/Awash Rock
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A concreted mass of stony material or coral which dries, is awash or is below the water surface.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Wreck
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The ruined remains of a stranded or sunken vessel which has been rendered useless.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Obstruction
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: In marine navigation, anything that hinders or prevents movement, particularly anything that endangers or prevents passage of a vessel. The term is usually used to refer to an isolated danger to navigation, such as a sunken rock or pinnacle. Examples of obstructions include: snags, stumps, wellheads, diffusers, cribs, fish havens, foul areas, foul grounds, booms, ice booms and ground tackle.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Foul Ground
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Areas over which it is safe to navigate but which should be avoided for anchoring, taking the ground or ground fishing.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Fishing Facility
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A structure for fishing purposes which can be an obstruction to ships in general. The position of these structures may vary frequently over time.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Marine Farm/Culture
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An assemblage of cages, nets, rafts and floats or posts where fish, including shellfish, are artificially cultivated.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Offshore Platform
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A permanent offshore structure, either fixed or floating.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Cable Submarine
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An assembly of wires or fibres, or a wire rope or chain, which has been laid underwater or buried beneath the seafloor.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Cable Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area which contains one or more submarine cables.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Pipeline Submarine/On Land
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A connected set of pipes for conveying liquids, slurries, or gases.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A pipeline is a string of interconnected pipes used for the transport of matter, nowadays mainly oil or gas (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 3857). It must be assumed that the pipes are vulnerable to damage from anchoring or trawling. They may be a potential danger to navigation (IHO Chart Specifications, M-4).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Submarine Pipeline Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area containing one or more submarine pipelines.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Offshore Production Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area at sea within which there are production facilities.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Navigation Line
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A straight line extending towards an area of navigational interest and generally generated by two navigational aids or one navigational aid and a bearing. For IENCs a navigation line either defines a recommended track or marks the boundary between a safe and a dangerous area.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The extent of the navigation line depends on the visibility of the navigational aid(s). The recommended track is that portion of a 'navigation line' that a ship should use for navigation.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Recommended Track
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A route which has been specially examined to ensure so far as possible that it is free of dangers and along which ships are advised to navigate. For IENCs it is a recommended sailing route for all or certain vessels.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Recommended tracks include all channels recommended for hydrographic reasons to lead safely between shoal depths. The use of such tracks is generally left to the discretion of the mariner and will depend on the vessel's draught, the state of the tide, adequacy of navigational aids and so on (IHO Chart Specifications, M-4). The recommended track is that portion of a 'navigation line' that a ship should use for navigation. In the case of a two-way recommended track only one value of orientation is encoded; the other value can be deduced (that is, the value encoded + 180 degrees).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Fairway
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: That part of a river, harbour and so on, where the main navigable channel for vessels of larger size lies. It is also the usual course followed by vessels entering or leaving harbours, called 'ship channel'. For IENCs the part of the navigable waterway area where a certain water depth within a certain width is available for the continuous navigation.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Fairway System
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: That part of a river, harbour and so on, where the main navigable channel for vessels of larger size lies. It is also the usual course followed by vessels entering or leaving harbours, called 'ship channel'. A fairway system is an aggregation of connected fairway features making up a complex fairway system.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A fairway system is composed of two or more Fairway features that comprise a complex fairway routeing system, for instance a long fairway comprising several bends.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Recommended Route Centreline
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The recommended route centreline indicates the 'centreline' of a recommended route.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A recommended route is a route of undefined width, for the convenience of ships in transit, which is often marked by centerline buoys (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 4448). A recommended route describes the regulation of navigation for non-hydrographic reasons such as the prevention of collision or the avoidance of pollution risks. It is generally laid down by a national or international authority other than the hydrographic authority. (IHO Chart Specifications, S-4)

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Two-Way Route Part
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area of a two-way route within which traffic flow is generally along one bearing (and possibly its reciprocal). For IENCs a two-way route part is either for the entire area, or a part of an area where the traffic flow is restricted to one-way.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The complete two-way route consists of one or more parts depending on the shape of the two-way route. The orientation of the two-way route part is defined by its centerline and is related to the general direction of the two-way route.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Two-Way Route
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A route within defined limits inside which two way traffic is established, aimed at providing safe passage of ships through waters where navigation is difficult or dangerous.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Recommended Traffic Lane Part
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A traffic flow pattern indicating a recommended directional movement of traffic where it is impractical or unnecessary to adopt an established direction of traffic flow.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Several Hydrographic Offices, in consultation with their Ministries of Transport, have added recommended directions in areas such as the outer approaches to major ports in order to show the best routes for crossing traffic or to minimize head-on encounters.(IHO Chart Specifications, M-4). The object 'recommended traffic lane part' indicates the recommended traffic flow, for example, between two TSS; in the entrance areas of a TSS; or beside a deep water route. The complete recommended traffic lane consists of one or more parts depending on the various shapes of the recommended traffic lane. The orientation of the recommended traffic lane part is defined by the middle-line of the recommended traffic lane part relating to the general direction of the recommended traffic lane part.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Inshore Traffic Zone
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A routeing measure comprising a designated area between the landward boundary of a traffic separation scheme and the adjacent coast, to be used in accordance with the provisions of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Precautionary Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A routeing measure comprising an area within defined limits where ships must navigate with particular caution and within which the direction of traffic flow may be recommended.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Traffic Separation Scheme Lane Part
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area within defined limits in which one-way traffic is established. Natural obstacles, including those forming separation zones, may constitute a boundary.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The complete traffic lane may consist of one or more lane parts depending on the shape of the lane.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Separation Zone or Line
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A zone or line separating the traffic lanes in which ships are proceeding in opposite, or nearly opposite directions; or separating a traffic lane from the adjacent sea area; or separating traffic lanes designated for particular classes of ships proceeding in the same direction.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Traffic Separation Scheme Boundary
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The outer limit of a traffic lane part or a traffic separation scheme roundabout.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Traffic Separation Scheme Crossing
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A defined area where traffic lanes cross.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Traffic Separation Scheme
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A routeing measure aimed at the separation of opposing streams of traffic by appropriate means and by the establishment of traffic lanes.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Radio Calling-In Point
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A designated position at which vessels are required to report to a traffic control centre. Also called reporting point or radio reporting point.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Radio calling-in points are established in certain busy waterways and port approaches to assist traffic control.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Ferry Route
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A route in a body of water where a ferry crosses from one shoreline to another.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Radar Line
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Recommended tracks along which ships can be guided by coastal radar stations in the event of bad visibility.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Radar Range
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Indicates the coverage of a sea area by a radar surveillance station. Inside this area a vessel may request shore-based radar assistance, particularly in poor visibility.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Many large ports have a radar surveillance system covering their approaches to provide guidance for vessels, particularly in poor visibility. The maximum range of the system forms an arc or series of overlapping arcs (IHO Chart Specifications, M-4).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Radar Station
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A station with a transmitter emitting pulses of ultra-high frequency radio waves which are reflected by solid objects and are detected upon their return to the sending station. For IENCs the radar station of a VTS or a lock to locate vessels and/ or monitor the traffic.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The feature 'radar station' is used to encode the technical equipment itself independent of the building or structure where it is installed. This building or structure, for example mast, tower, building, radar dome is a different feature.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Anchorage Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area in which vessels or seaplanes anchor or may anchor.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Mooring Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area in which vessels may be secured to mooring buoys.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Anchor Berth
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A designated area of water where a vessel, sea plane, etc., may anchor. For IENCs a designated area of water where a single vessel, convoy, sea plane, etc. may anchor.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: In general the anchor berth is defined by the centre point and a swinging circle radius.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Seaplane Landing Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A designated portion of water for the landing and take-off of seaplanes.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Dumping Ground
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A sea area where dredged material or other potentially more harmful material, for example explosives, chemical waste, is deliberately deposited.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Military Practice Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area within which naval, military or aerial exercises are carried out.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Administration Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A defined area within which a jurisdiction applies. It may or may not be named. For IENCs a defined and named administrative area (e.g. country, state, district) or a defined and named administrative area of a river surveillance

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Cargo Transhipment Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area designated for transfer of cargo from one vessel to another sometimes in order to reduce a vessel's draught.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The transhipment of cargo is often known as 'lightering' and the area may be known as 'lightering area' or 'cargo transfer area'.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Caution Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Generally, an area where the mariner has to be made aware of circumstances influencing the safety of navigation.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: This may be required to identify: a danger, a risk, a rule, or advice -- which is not directly related to a specific object.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Information Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area for which general information regarding navigation, but not directly related to safety of navigation, is available.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Custom Zone
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The area within which national custom regulations are in force.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Fishery Zone
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The offshore zone in which exclusive fishing rights and management are held by the coastal nation.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The fishery zone commonly coincides with other zones such as: Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Free Port Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A port where certain import and export duties are waived (unless goods pass into the country) to facilitate reshipment to other countries.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Harbour Area (Administrative)
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The area over which a harbour authority has jurisdiction. For IENCs the area of water and land with the works necessary for its formation, protection and maintenance.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Oil Barrier
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A floating barrier to stop and contain the spread of oil on a water body surface. For IENCs any construction to dam oil flow on water.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Straight Territorial Sea Baseline
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Straight baselines are a system of straight lines joining specified or discrete points on the low-water line, usually known as straight baseline turning points. Straight baselines are used in delimitation.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Pilotage District
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area within which a pilotage direction exists. Such directions are regulated by a competent harbour authority which dictates circumstances under which they apply.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Collision Regulations Limit
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972 (COLREGs). The demarcation line between inland navigation rules and international navigation rules.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Restricted Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by an appropriate authority within which navigation is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions. For IENCs restricted areas typically surround dams; see 8.12 Dams.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Light All Around
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An all around light is a light that is visible over the whole horizon of interest to marine navigation and having no change in the characteristics of the light.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Light Sectored
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A light presenting different appearances (in particular, different colours) over various parts of the horizon of interest to maritime navigation.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Light Air Obstruction
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An air obstruction light is a light marking an obstacle which constitutes a danger to air navigation.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Lateral Buoy
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A lateral buoy is used to indicate the port or starboard hand side of the route to be followed. They are generally used for well-defined channels and are used in conjunction with a conventional direction of buoyage. For IENCs this includes: -Buoys at bifurcations of channels (A buoy at a fairway junction may indicate by its top mark on which side it is preferable to pass (main channel)).- Buoys at bridge pillars (A buoy at a bridge pillar may be used to improve the visibility of the pillar location on the radar.)- Buoys marking danger points (Buoys to indicate the presence of potentially dangerous obstructions such as groins, banks, or wrecks.)- Stalling buoys (The buoys (floating beacons) are used to mark stalling current which does not coincide with a direction of the fairway.)- Swinging lateral buoys (The buoys are used to mark swinging points at the edges of the extended rectilinear fairways, as well as at the fairway edges where the vision is limited.)
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A buoy is a floating object moored to the bottom in a particular place, as an aid to navigation or for other specific purposes. (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 565). Light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Cardinal Buoy
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A cardinal buoy is used in conjunction with the compass to indicate where the mariner may find the best navigable water. It is placed in one of the four quadrants (North, East, South and West), bounded by inter-cardinal bearings from the point marked. For IENCs a cardinal buoy is used to mark the position of danger points, obstacles and special features on lakes and broad waterways.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A buoy is a floating object moored to the bottom in a particular place, as an aid to navigation or for other specific purposes. (IHO Dictionary S-32 5th Edition, 565). Topmark, light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Isolated Danger Buoy
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An isolated danger buoy is a buoy moored on or above an isolated danger of limited extent, which has navigable water all around it.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A buoy is a floating object moored to the bottom in a particular place, as an aid to navigation or for other specific purposes. (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 565). Topmark, light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Safe Water Buoy
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A safe water buoy is used to indicate that there is navigable water around the mark. For IENCs a safe water buoy marking the axis or middle of a channel may be used as a centerline, mid-channel on lakes and broad waterways. The swinging axial buoys are used to mark swinging points of the fairway axis.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A buoy is a floating object moored to the bottom in a particular place, as an aid to navigation or for other specific purposes. (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 565). Topmark, light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Special Purpose/General Buoy
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A special purpose buoy is primarily used to indicate an area or feature, the nature of which is apparent from reference to a chart, Sailing Directions or Notices to Mariners. For IENCs also buoys to indicate the presence of potentially dangerous obstructions such as groins, banks, or wrecks, buoys to be used as initial marking of a dangerous wreck and supporting pontoons of swinging wire ferries
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A buoy is a floating object moored to the bottom in a particular place, as an aid to navigation or for other specific purposes. (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 565). Light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Emergency Wreck Marking Buoy
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An emergency wreck marking buoy is a buoy moored on or above a new wreck, designed to provide a prominent (both visual and radio) and easily identifiable temporary first response.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Installation Buoy
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An installation buoy is a buoy used for loading tankers with gas or oil.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A buoy is a floating object moored to the bottom in a particular place, as an aid to navigation or for other specific purposes. (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 565).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Mooring Buoy
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A buoy secured to the bottom by permanent moorings with means for mooring a vessel by use of its anchor chain or mooring lines.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Lateral Beacon
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A lateral beacon is used to indicate the port or starboard hand side of the route to be followed. They are generally used for well defined channels and are used in conjunction with a conventional direction of buoyage. For IENCs also beacons that are used to mark specific “Landmarks” and submerged banks.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A beacon is a prominent specially constructed object forming a conspicuous mark as a fixed aid to navigation or for use in hydrographic survey (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 420). Light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Cardinal Beacon
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A cardinal beacon is used in conjunction with the compass to indicate where the mariner may find the best navigable water. It is placed in one of the four quadrants (North, East, South and West), bounded by inter-cardinal bearings from the point marked.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A beacon is a prominent specially constructed object forming a conspicuous mark as a fixed aid to navigation or for use in hydrographic survey (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 420). Light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Isolated Danger Beacon
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An isolated danger beacon is a beacon erected on an isolated danger of limited extent, which has navigable water all around it.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A beacon is a prominent specially constructed object forming a conspicuous mark as a fixed aid to navigation or for use in hydrographic survey (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 420). Light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Safe Water Beacon
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A safe water beacon is used to indicate that there is navigable water around the mark.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A beacon is a prominent specially constructed object forming a conspicuous mark as a fixed aid to navigation or for use in hydrographic survey (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 420). Light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Special Purpose/General Beacon
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A special purpose beacon is primarily used to indicate an area or feature, the nature of which is apparent from reference to a chart, Sailing Directions or Notices to Mariners.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A beacon is a prominent specially constructed object forming a conspicuous mark as a fixed aid to navigation or for use in hydrographic survey (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition, 420). Light, fog signal, radar reflector and retro-reflector are separate features.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Daymark
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: (1) The identifying characteristics of an aid to navigation which serve to facilitate its recognition against a daylight viewing background. On those structures that do not by themselves present an adequate viewing area to be seen at the required distance, the aid is made more visible by affixing a daymark to the structure. A daymark so affixed has a distinctive colour and shape depending on the purpose of the aid. (2) An unlighted navigational mark. For IENCs daymarks are used to code passing and crossing day beacons on the inland river system.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Radar Reflector
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A device capable of, or intended for, reflecting radar signals.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A radar reflector is usually a tetrahedron or pentagonal corner reflector to facilitate reflection towards the sender (International Maritime Dictionary, 2nd Ed.).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Fog Signal
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A warning signal transmitted by a vessel, or aid to navigation, during periods of low visibility. Also, the device producing such a signal.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Buoy Line
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A buoy line is a set of buoys positioned on a curve indicating a certain restriction.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Physical AIS Aid to Navigation
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An Automatic Identification System (AIS) message 21 transmitted from a physical Aid to Navigation, or transmitted from an AIS station for an Aid to Navigation which physically exists.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Radio Station
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A place equipped to transmit radio waves. Such a station may be either stationary or mobile, and may also be provided with a radio receiver.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The transmission of a radio station may serve to provide mariners with a line of position (IHO Chart Specifications, M-4). The feature 'radio station' is used to encode the point of transmission of the signal.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Radar Transponder Beacon
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A transponder beacon transmitting a coded signal on radar frequency, permitting an interrogating craft to determine the bearing and range of the transponder. For IENCs a radar transponder beacon (racon) may be used to indicate an entrance of a canal or a bridge passage.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The feature 'radar transponder beacon' is only used to encode the technical equipment independent of the structure on which it is located (for example a beacon, light-vessel or tower).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Pilot Boarding Place
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A location offshore where a pilot may board a vessel in preparation to piloting it through local waters.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Vessel Traffic Service Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The area of any service implemented by a relevant authority primarily designed to improve safety and efficiency of traffic flow and the protection of the environment. It may range from simple information messages, to extensive organisation of the traffic involving national or regional schemes.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Coast Guard Station
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A station at which a visual/radio/radar marine watch is kept either continuously or at certain times only.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: This feature is used to describe the function of the coastguard rather than the building in which the coastguard is sited.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Signal Station Warning
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A warning signal station is a place on shore from which warning signals are made to ships at sea. For IENCs this includes: - Depth Indicator: Device that shows the real water depth between the actual water level and the bottom of the waterway or isolated dangers under water (e.g., ground sill). - The manner in which the device indicates this can either be analog (e.g., by a water level staff / pole - one can read the real water depth directly at the water level) or digital (e.g. by a display). - External indicator of a gauge, also if the indicator is not directly located at the gauge – this is not the same as a depth indicator (values at gauges are always referred to the zero point of the gauge). - High Water Mark: Device that shows if official high water levels are reached. This can be indicated either by analogue (e.g., by signs like a staff gauge) or digital (e.g., by a display).- A signal station showing a warning if an outlet of water (e.g. from a pumping station) causes a current.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Signal Station Traffic
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A traffic signal station is a place on shore from which signals are made to regulate the movement of traffic. For IENCs this includes: - Bridge passage signal station: a place on shore from which signals are made for the control of vessels wishing to pass under a bridge. - Lock signal station: a place on shore from which signals are made for the control of vessels entering or leaving a lock. - Oncoming traffic indicator: a place on shore from which signals are made to inform about oncoming traffic. - Port entry and departure: a place on shore from which signals are made for the control of vessels entering or leaving a port.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: A signal station is a place on shore from which signals are made to ships at sea (IHO Dictionary, S-32, 5th Edition).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Rescue Station
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A place where equipment for saving life at sea is maintained.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Encodes the service available at this location. The structure housing the service should be encoded separately.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Harbour Facility
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A harbour installation with a service or commercial operation of public interest.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Small Craft Facility
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A place at which a service generally of interest to small craft or pleasure boats is available.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: Encodes the service available at this location. The structure housing the service should be encoded separately.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Text Placement
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The Text Placement feature is used in association with the Feature Name attribute or a light description to optimize text positioning in ECDIS.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Bunker Station
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A station, at which a ship is able to bunker fuel, water or ballast or to obtain electrical power supply.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Communication Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Indicates the coverage of an area, in which a vessel has to report or may request information.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Exceptional Navigation Structure
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An exceptional navigational construction like aqueduct, lift-lock, etc.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Harbour Basin
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An enclosed area of water surrounded by quay walls constructed to provide means for the transfer of cargos from and to ships.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Lock Basin Part
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A lock basin is divided into several lock basin parts, if this lock basin has one ground level but several gates.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Maximum Permitted Ship Dimensions
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Waterway or waterway section for which a juridical regulation with respect to the maximum permitted vessel dimensions exists.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Maximum Permitted Vessel Speed
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Waterway or waterway section for which a juridical regulation with respect to the maximum permitted vessel speed exists.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Notice Mark
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A notice board or sign indicating information to the mariner.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Port Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: Apart from harbours a port includes a city or borough with accommodation and facilities for landing passengers and goods and some amount of overseas trade. A port may possess a harbour but a harbour is not necessarily a port.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Refuse Dump
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: At a refuse dump ships are able to unload their refuse like waste oil or black water.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Sensor
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A device that responds to a physical stimulus (as heat, light, sound, pressure, magnetism or a particular motion) and transmits a resulting impulse (as for measurement or operating a control).

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Terminal
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A terminal covers that area on shore which provides buildings and constructions for the transfer of cargo or passengers from and to ships.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Turning Basin
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area of water or enlargement of a channel used for turning vessels.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Vehicle Transfer
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A place where vehicles can be loaded or unloaded from the inland vessel with onboard or on-shore facilities.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Waterway Area
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An area in which uniform general information of the waterway exists.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Waterway Axis
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: The waterway axis can be defined as, for example: - The middle line of a fairway, (Definition of fairway: That part of a river, harbour; etc. where the main navigable channel for vessels of larger size lies. It is also the usual course followed by vessels entering or leaving harbours, called "ship channel". (International Maritime Dictionary, 2nd Ed.)). - The middle line of a water way (Definition of waterway: The waterway covers the entire area of a river or canal).
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: The object name indicates the specific name of a public waterway/or part of waterway.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Waterway Gauge
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: An instrument for measuring water levels.
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:remarks: This object is needed in order to develop a unique and standardized way of providing data and information about gauges on inland waterways. This way is a precondition of including information on actual water levels in order to refer depth data as well as vertical clearances at bridges etc. to the present situation on waterways.

S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:name: Waterway Profile
S100FC:S100_FC_FeatureType.S100FC:definition: A physically non-existent line which is normally the connection of two opposite distance marks. Waterway profiles can be used to define a special water level.
